PE1.title: Physical Education 1: Foundations and Phases
PE1.summary: A comprehensive overview of Physical Education covering its history, definitions, college requirements, domains of learning, objectives, and distinct phases including swimming, dances, gymnastics, games, sports, and recreational activities.
PE1.content:
Its Values to the Development and Adjustment of the Individual

Modern Physical Education activities are based on the natural education of primitive times. Even more recent activities, when analyzed, are found to be developed from natural activities. In most educational systems, physical education—also called physical training or gym, though each has a very different connotation—is a course in the curriculum which utilizes learning in the cognitive, affective, and psychomotor domains in a play or movement exploration setting. The term physical education is commonly used in this way; however, notes signify that 'they participated in the subject are not studied it'.

Physical Education has existed since the earliest stages of humanity, in areas as simple as the transmission of knowledge of basic survival skills, such as hunting. However, the real history of physical education lies in the changing methodologies used to transmit physical skills and, to a lesser extent, the varying intentions of the educator.

The first known literary reference to an athletic competition is preserved in the ancient Greek text, the Iliad by Homer. While by no means the beginning of physical activity, it marks an important point in the study of the history of physical education. Other cultures that existed before the Greeks, including ancient Chinese, Indian, and Egyptian civilizations, had traditions of physical education and activity; however, the Greek influence is argued to be the most fundamental to how the discipline is viewed today. The Ancient Greek tradition of the Olympic Games, which originated in the early 8th century BC, continues today. The father of Modern Physical Education as known today was Friedrich Ludwig Jahn. Although Jahn was highly political within Germany, his contributions to physical education—mostly in gymnastics as a discipline—are still seen today.

What is Physical Education?

Physical education is the interdisciplinary study of all areas of science relating to the transmission of physical knowledge and skills to an individual or a group, the application of these skills, and their results.

Physical Education is an important segment of general education which aims to contribute to the total development of the learner through participation in selected activities. It provides opportunities to acquire lifelong skills that are essential to physical, mental, social, and emotional development.

It can also be viewed as a program of activities in a school curriculum that involves sports, games, dance, gymnastics, and recreational activities. Great emphasis is placed on motor skills, fitness, health, recreation, and safety. It is a vital and integral part of general education designed to promote the optimum development of the individual physically, socially, emotionally, and mentally through total movement in the performance of properly selected physical activities.

Physical Education in College

Service Physical Education refers to the four subjects given to freshmen and sophomores in the first four semesters of their college work as stipulated in DECS Order No. 58, series of 1990:

  • Physical Education 1: Physical Fitness and Self-Testing Activities – Covers the essentials of physical fitness components and self-testing activities.
  • Physical Education 2: Rhythmic Activities – Focuses on rhythm, fundamental rhythmic activities, dance mixers, local and foreign dances, as well as social dances.
  • Physical Education 3: Individual and Dual Sports / Games – Deals with the acquisition of skills in recreational activities such as bowling, table tennis, badminton, track and field events, and fosters love of country by including Mga Laro ng Lahi.
  • Physical Education 4: Team Sports – Emphasizes the acquisition of the fundamentals of common team sports such as volleyball, basketball, and baseball/softball.

Core Frameworks

3 Domains of Learning

  • Psychomotor
  • Cognitive
  • Affective

4 Objectives of P.E.

  • Emotional
  • Social
  • Mental
  • Physical

Phases of Physical Education

1. Swimming

  • Freestyle – Most efficient stroke.
  • Backstroke
  • Breast stroke
  • Butterfly stroke – Most demanding.
  • Dog Paddle – First ever stroke made or done.
  • 20x50 – Official swimming pool size.
  • 10ft – Adequate depth for diving.

2. Dances

  • Folk Dance – Includes national dance and local dance.
  • Tribal Dance
  • Ritual Dance – Associated with Gods and Goddesses.
  • Ethnic Dance – Uses brass-type instruments.
  • Ballroom Dance / Social Dance – Includes Standard and Latin dances.
  • Modern Dance – Includes hiphop, wave, and punk.
  • Jazz
  • Ballet

3. Self-Testing Activities

  • Stunts
  • Tumbling ('Humbling')
  • Pyramid building

4. Gymnastics

  • Rhythmic Gymnastics – Uses light apparatus such as ribbons, wands, hoops, balls, and rings.
  • Artistic Gymnastics – Uses heavy apparatus such as pommel horse, balance beam, vaulting box, horizontal bar, and rings.

5. Games

  • Laro ng Lahi – Traditional Filipino Games including tumbang preso, kadang kadang, luksong baka, and luksong tinik.
  • Indigenous Games – Mind Games including scrabble, games of the general, and chess.
  • Parlor Games – Includes trip to Jerusalem, newspaper dance, and egg relay.

6. Individual and Dual Sports

  • Individual Sports – Track and Field (running, jumping, throwing events), Swimming, Cycling, Gymnastics, Equestrian, Archery, Bowling, Weight lifting, Diving.
  • Dual Sports – Lawn Tennis, Table Tennis, Badminton, Fencing, Chess.

7. Team Sports

  • Basketball, Volleyball, Baseball, Softball, Soccer, Beach Volleyball, Sepak Takraw, Rugby.

8. Combative Sports

  • Wrestling, Taekwondo, Boxing, Karate.

9. Recreational Activities

Derived from Latin. Includes:

  • Dancing
  • Cooking
  • Singing
  • Gardening
  • Collections
  • Outing
